items.title: WO-304 APPROVED after 3 attempts: Raise the single-bolus limit to 25 U
items.text: Work order WO-304 (insulin-pump): Raise the single-bolus limit to 25 U. Verdict: APPROVED after 3 attempts. Attempt 1 (the obvious one-line patch, MAX_BOLUS_U 10 -> 25 U): BLOCKED for SR-1 (H-1); world model: 4 new severe-hypo runs. Attempt 2: BLOCKED for world model: 2 new severe-hypo runs. Attempt 3: passed all checks. Fix that passed the gate: large meals for adults are spread over time. The 10 U single-bolus cap (SR-1) is unchanged; per-hour delivery stays <= MAX_BOLUS_RATE_UPH, SR-2 daily cap and SR-3 low-BG lockout still apply. Evidence: 5 requirements tested, 5 passed; world model PASS: 0 new severe-hypo runs in 20 simulations, 2 pre-existing.

items.text: Mitigated by SR-5: Watchdog alarm after 2000 ms without heartbeat. Source: demo/pump/safety.json.

items.title: FDA premarket guidance: device software functions
items.text: Content of premarket submissions for device software functions: a pump that can cause serious injury needs Enhanced documentation level, including software requirements, architecture, risk management file, traceability between requirements, hazards and tests, unresolved anomalies and the verification and validation results for every change.

items.title: IEC 60601-2-24: infusion pumps and controllers
items.text: Particular safety standard for infusion pumps: protection against over-infusion and under-infusion, bolus volume accuracy, occlusion alarm and its response time, and alarms for faults that stop delivery. Limits on bolus size and rate are protective measures and must not be bypassed by a new delivery mode.

items.title: ISO 14971: risk management for medical devices
items.text: Identify hazards and hazardous situations, estimate and evaluate risk, implement risk control measures, verify that each control is implemented and effective, and evaluate residual risk. A software change that touches a risk control (a dose limit, a lockout, an alarm) must re-verify that control and update the risk management file.

items.title: IEC 62304: medical device software life cycle (Class C)
items.text: Insulin pump firmware is software safety Class C (death or serious injury possible). Class C requires software requirements traced to risk controls, detailed design, unit implementation and verification, integration and system testing, regression testing after every change, configuration management and a problem resolution process. Every change needs a change request, impact analysis on existing risk controls and re-verification evidence.

items.title: demo/pump/pump.c dependency map
items.text: request_bolus checks MAX_BOLUS_U (SR-1), MIN_BG_FOR_BOLUS (SR-3) and MAX_DAILY_U via delivered_today_u (SR-2). check_occlusion uses OCCLUSION_KPA (SR-4). check_watchdog uses WATCHDOG_MS (SR-5). Any edit to pump.h constants affects every requirement that reads it.

items.title: Open finding: insulin-sensitive patients and decimal slips
items.text: World model on main: for insulin-sensitive patients (carb ratio 16 to 22) a 10x typo stays under the 10 U cap and causes severe hypoglycemia. Proposed SR-6: cap a single bolus relative to the patient's configured carb ratio.

items.title: Email from regulatory affairs: IEC 62304 evidence
items.text: For the next submission every software change to the bolus path needs: hazard analysis update (ISO 14971), traceability from requirement to test, and verification evidence. Simulation evidence from a validated patient model (UVA/Padova) is accepted as supporting evidence.

items.title: #pump-firmware Slack thread
items.text: Product asked for bigger meal boluses for adult users with high insulin needs (carb ratio 5). Firmware lead: OK only if per-hour delivery stays within the max bolus rate and the daily cap of 60 U still applies.

items.title: Clinical safety review, Oct 28 (transcript summary)
items.text: Clinical lead: never raise the 10 U single-bolus cap. Large meals should use an extended or dual-wave bolus delivered over time. Typing errors (decimal slips) are the top real-world overdose cause in pump incident reports.

items.title: WO-7 (closed): Add 2000 ms controller watchdog
items.text: Past work order. Added WATCHDOG_MS 2000 and check_watchdog to stop runaway delivery when the controller hangs (H-5). Lesson: any change to timing constants needs SR-5 re-verified.
